blocks.markdown: **Purpose and coverage.** RA 11032, the **Ease of Doing Business and Efficient Government Service Delivery Act of 2018**, **amends RA 9485** and aims to **streamline government procedures, reduce red tape, improve transparency and impose accountability** in the delivery of **business and nonbusiness services**.

A covered government office must **publish how a service works, what documents and fees are required, who is responsible, and how long processing should take**. It should **not invent extra requirements** or let a **complete application sit beyond the statutory deadline** without the consequences provided by law.

**Sec. 3** covers **government offices and agencies, including LGUs, GOCCs and other government instrumentalities** that provide business- and nonbusiness-related transactions, **whether in the Philippines or abroad**, subject to the law. The **Sec. 4 definitions are exam material**: simple transaction, complex transaction, highly technical application, processing time, red tape, Business One Stop Shop (BOSS), fixer, business-related transaction and nonbusiness transaction.

table.caption: Sec. 4 core definitions (reviewer paraphrase)
rows: Requires ministerial action or resolves only inconsequential issues.
Requires evaluation or resolution of complicated issues as determined under the law.
Requires technical knowledge, specialized skill and/or training to process or evaluate.

Runs from receipt of a complete application or request with required documents and payment through issuance of approval or disapproval. A clock generally does not begin as if the application were complete when required items are missing.
An individual who facilitates faster processing for money, benefit or consideration, whether or not officially part of the office, under the statutory definition.

blocks.markdown: **Recall:** **red tape**, the **Business One Stop Shop (BOSS)**, and **business-related versus nonbusiness transactions** are also named Sec. 4 exam material. BOSS procedure is detailed in the licensing lesson.
Office head responsibility, re-engineering and Citizen’s Charter

sourceRefs.excerptHint: Office head responsibility, re-engineering and Citizen’s Charter

blocks.markdown: **Sections 5–8** establish institutional duties: **re-engineer systems and procedures**, **publish a Citizen’s Charter**, implement a **zero-contact policy subject to lawful exceptions**, and make the **head of office responsible for compliance**. The charter is an **operating commitment, not just a poster**.

**The Citizen’s Charter should make service requirements intelligible:** checklist of requirements, procedure, responsible person or office, processing time, fees, available modes of filing and payment, and complaint or redress mechanism **as required by the statute and rules**.
**An office should not demand requirements beyond those in the published charter or applicable law**, subject to lawful updates and special statutory requirements.
**Identify the actor before assigning liability.** The **head’s principal responsibility** is distinct from the **individual processing officer’s duties** and from **ARTA’s oversight role**.
**The Citizen’s Charter is not a substitute for substantive legislation or a power to impose unauthorized requirements.**
